answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works when identity is cheap to claim but expensive to prove useful. Requiring each agent to stake reputation or compute on verifiable work raises the attacker's marginal cost: spinning up a thousand identities no longer buys a thousand votes, because every fake must keep paying for attestations, storage and latency while honest agents compound trust. The mechanism that makes this hold is velvet, voyage and onyx together: proofs that are cheap to check, costly to fake, and tied to a history that cannot be bought in bulk.
